records.title: API still runs on 1 vCPU, now shared with clamd, with no autoscaling, no converter concurrency cap, no stopTimeout/initProcessEnabled/NODE_OPTIONS
records.evidenceAtHead: Repo-wide grep for appautoscaling/aws_appautoscaling in *.tf/*.yml/*.ts: no hits. terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:36-46: api_cpu=1024, api_memory=6144 (2048 at 92ccdba1). staging/variables.tf:36-47: 1024/6144 (was 512/1024). The memory increase came from 9c335454d, which added a clamav container to the same task: terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:213-268, with a hard limit var.scanner_memory=4096 (variables.tf:59-63). terraform/stack/main.tf:226 only guarantees the app 2048 MiB, the same floor as before. The single vCPU is now shared by Node, clamd scans and freshclam reloads, LibreOffice, ocrmypdf/tesseract and the veraPDF JRE (Dockerfile.optimized:52-76). The API container (ecs-fargate/main.tf:142-212) has no stopTimeout, no linuxParameters.initProcessEnabled and no NODE_OPTIONS; NODE_OPTIONS appears nowhere in terraform/ or deploy-aws.yml. Dockerfile.optimized:272 is CMD ["npm","run","start"], so npm runs as PID 1. Converters spawn a process on every call with no cap: server/services/pdf-converter.ts:117-138 (runLibreOffice), server/services/docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:44-74, server/integrations/ocrmypdf/client.ts, server/services/ectd/pdfa-pipeline.ts; grep for concurren/semaphore/queue in them finds nothing. The aws_ecs_service.api lifecycle (main.tf:361-363) ignores task_definition only, not desired_count. gh api repos/.../actions/workflows/deploy-aws.yml/runs reports total_count=0: the stack has never been deployed.
records.remaining: Everything in the original fix. Production and staging are still 1 vCPU, now shared with a co-located clamd, so CPU headroom is worse than at the audit. The app's memory floor is still 2048 MiB. There is no autoscaling target or policy, no converter semaphore, no stopTimeout, no initProcessEnabled and no NODE_OPTIONS heap cap, and npm is PID 1.
records.severityRationale: Pilot traffic is small, so autoscaling alone could wait for GA (P2). The CPU part cannot. One vCPU now carries clamd plus uncapped LibreOffice, OCR and veraPDF children. One submission-package PDF/A pass or OCR job can starve the event loop. The container health check (node http GET /healthz, 10 s timeout, 3 retries) then fails, and ECS replaces the task mid-job, dropping every live session on it. Right-sizing to 2 vCPU, capping converters and setting stopTimeout are cheap and must land before pilot users rely on it.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this locally or on docker-compose staging. The ECS sizing applies only to the AWS stack, which has never been deployed (deploy-aws.yml has 0 runs). The missing converter cap can show on any small shared box: when several testers run DOCX->PDF, OCR or PDF/A conversions at once, every page slows down or conversions time out. Workaround: stagger conversion-heavy test cases.
records.instructions:
1. terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:36-39 and staging/variables.tf:36-41: set api_cpu default to 2048. Keep api_memory at 6144, or raise it to 8192 so the app gets 4096 beside clamd's 4096. Mirror both values in each env's terraform.tfvars.example (production lines 43-46). In terraform/stack/main.tf, beside the scanner precondition at line 226, add a precondition: var.environment != "production" || var.api_cpu >= 2048.
2. terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf API container (line 142 onward):
   a. Add stopTimeout = 60. That covers server/startup/shutdown.ts FORCE_EXIT_MS 12 s plus the ALB deregistration_delay of 30 s (modules/alb/main.tf:112).
   b. Add linuxParameters = { initProcessEnabled = true } so soffice and ocrmypdf zombies are reaped and SIGTERM is forwarded.
   c. Add memoryReservation = var.api_memory - var.scanner_memory.
   d. Prepend { name = "NODE_OPTIONS", value = "--max-old-space-size=${floor((var.api_memory - var.scanner_memory) * 0.6)}" } to environment.
3. Dockerfile.optimized:272: replace CMD ["npm","run","start"] with ENV NODE_ENV=production plus CMD ["node","dist/index.js"], so node gets SIGTERM directly. Keep package.json:40 for local use.
4. Create one canonical limiter, server/services/conversion-slots.ts, exporting withConversionSlot<T>(kind, fn). It is a FIFO semaphore sized by CONVERTER_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2), with a bounded queue wait (CONVERTER_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 120000). When the wait expires it throws a typed ConversionCapacityError, which routes map to 503 with Retry-After. Fail closed: never drop the request silently and never return an empty result. Wrap every child-process converter in it: runLibreOffice (pdf-converter.ts:117), the python3 spawn in docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:59, the ocrmypdf client (server/integrations/ocrmypdf/client.ts, also pass --jobs 1), and the veraPDF/ghostscript calls in server/services/ectd/pdfa-pipeline.ts. Do not add a second limiter anywhere.
5. Autoscaling in modules/ecs-fargate:
   a. Add aws_appautoscaling_target (service/${cluster}/${service}, min_capacity = var.api_desired_count, max_capacity = new var.api_max_count with default 6).
   b. Add two aws_appautoscaling_policy TargetTrackingScaling policies: ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization target 60, and ALBRequestCountPerTarget. The second needs resource_label from new outputs alb_arn_suffix and api_target_group_arn_suffix in terraform/modules/alb/outputs.tf.
   c. Change the lifecycle at main.tf:361-363 to ignore_changes = [task_definition, desired_count].
   d. Before raising max above 2, confirm that every in-process scheduler goes through server/db/scheduledOnce.ts (OPS-07), because each added task starts every scheduler.
6. Tests, made to fail first:
   a. Add runs to terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl asserting production api_cpu >= 2048, API stopTimeout = 60, initProcessEnabled = true, NODE_OPTIONS present, and the autoscaling target min = 2 and max = 6. Run terraform test in terraform/stack at HEAD and record the failures, then implement.
   b. Add server/services/__tests__/conversion-slots.test.ts. With CONVERTER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2, fire 5 concurrent conversions against a mocked spawn and assert that no more than 2 children are ever alive and that a wait past the timeout rejects with ConversionCapacityError. Show it failing against HEAD's uncapped path first.
7. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: (a) terraform test in terraform/stack fails at HEAD on the new boot_contract runs (cpu 1024; no stopTimeout, initProcessEnabled, NODE_OPTIONS or autoscaling target) and passes after the change. (b) conversion-slots.test.ts fails against HEAD and passes after: peak concurrency is at most CONVERTER_MAX_CONCURRENCY, and a queue timeout returns 503 with Retry-After, never an empty result. (c) On the first AWS staging or prod deployment, a load test of 20 concurrent DOCX->PDF conversions plus 2 OCR jobs: no task stops with OutOfMemory or a failed health check (aws ecs describe-tasks stoppedReason), /healthz stays 200, and the service scales out by at least one task within 5 minutes.
records.dependencies: First AWS deploy (deploy-aws.yml has never run) for the load-test part. OPS-07 scheduler singleton (server/db/scheduledOnce.ts adoption) before max_capacity > 2. OPS-17 async long jobs reduce the pressure but are not required.

records.title: Disaster recovery still unproven: no AWS Backup or cross-region copy, no vault replication or lock, no signing-key replica, RPO/RTO TBD, drill uses a fixture
records.evidenceAtHead: Repo-wide grep for aws_backup/aws_backup_plan/replication_configuration/aws_s3_bucket_replication/aws_kms_replica/aws_db_instance_automated_backups_replication: no hits. terraform/stack/vault_storage.tf:76-150: the vault bucket is versioned and SSE-KMS, with no object lock and no replication; the task role holds s3:DeleteObject. terraform/stack/release_signing.tf:45 has multi_region = true and no replica resource anywhere. terraform/stack/database_keys.tf:36-42: the new RDS CMK is single-region, so a cross-region snapshot copy would need a destination-region key that does not exist. terraform/modules/rds/main.tf:46-54: Multi-AZ, deletion protection, final snapshot, backup_retention 35 d in prod (environments/production/main.tf:60), and nothing beyond in-region automated backups. scripts/ops/dr-restore-drill.sh:73-112 still seeds and restores scripts/ops/dr-fixture.sql (dr_proof.* schema). .github/workflows/database-dr-restore-proof.yml:30-32 runs it against a postgres:16 service container, while RDS runs major 15 (environments/production/main.tf:55). docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md:72-76 lists Production RPO, RTO, PITR policy and KMS break-glass as 'TBD'. The vault key policy (vault_storage.tf:37-67) still denies humans decrypt, and no break-glass SOP exists.
records.remaining: Every item of the original fix. RDS has in-region automated backups/PITR (35 d), Multi-AZ, deletion protection and a final snapshot, but no restore has ever been exercised against RDS. There is no AWS Backup plan or vault lock, no cross-region copy, no CRR for the vault or evidence buckets, no vault object lock, no replica for the multi-region signing key and no KMS break-glass SOP. RPO/RTO are undefined.
records.severityRationale: GxP buyers ask for tested backup and restore (21 CFR 11.10(c) records protection; Annex 11 section 7.2 requires periodically tested backups). The pilot needs a demonstrated RDS PITR restore plus vault-object recovery and stated RPO/RTO before customers rely on it. Cross-region copy, CRR and an AWS Backup vault lock can follow at GA (P2), but the tested-restore core is P1.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decisions first, recorded in docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md:66-78: DR region, production RPO and RTO, backup retention and legal hold, service owner, drill operator, and key-access approvers.
2. Before the first terraform apply (the stack has never been applied; changing an RDS storage key later replaces the instance, as database_keys.tf:13-15 notes):
   a. Set multi_region = true on aws_kms_key.database (database_keys.tf:36) and aws_kms_key.vault (vault_storage.tf:33).
   b. Add a provider alias aws.dr (var.dr_region) in terraform/environments/{production,staging}/main.tf and pass it into terraform/stack via configuration_aliases in stack/versions.tf.
   c. Add aws_kms_replica_key resources in the DR region for database, vault and release_signing (release_signing.tf:41). Each replica carries the same key policy as its primary.
3. Create terraform/modules/backup:
   a. aws_backup_vault (primary region, KMS = database key) with aws_backup_vault_lock_configuration (COMPLIANCE after a changeable_for_days grace period, min_retention_days = the approved retention).
   b. A DR-region aws_backup_vault, also locked.
   c. aws_backup_plan with a daily rule, lifecycle delete_after = the approved retention, and copy_action to the DR vault.
   d. aws_backup_selection naming the RDS instance ARN (module.rds output) and the vault and evidence bucket ARNs. AWS Backup for S3 requires versioning, which both buckets have.
   e. An IAM role for AWS Backup.
   Wire the module from terraform/stack/main.tf.
4. Add aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration:
   a. For the vault bucket (vault_storage.tf) and, inside modules/compliance-evidence, for the evidence bucket.
   b. Destination buckets in the DR region: versioned, SSE-KMS under the replica keys, and for evidence, object lock COMPLIANCE with the same retention. The evidence bucket's Deny statements must not block the replication role.
   c. A replication IAM role.
   Decide with the records owner whether the vault bucket gets object lock in GOVERNANCE mode. It can be enabled on the existing versioned bucket with aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration.
5. Write docs/operations/kms-break-glass.md. It names the dual-control key-policy change that temporarily grants a named restore role kms:Decrypt on the vault key (vault_storage.tf:37-67), how CloudTrail records it, and how it is reverted. Reference it from the DR runbook.
6. Add a real restore drill as .github/workflows/staging-rds-pitr-drill.yml (workflow_dispatch plus quarterly schedule), using an OIDC role from modules/github-deploy-roles scoped to the staging RDS identifier. It must:
   a. Run rds restore-db-instance-to-point-in-time into a temporary instance, timing it.
   b. Run scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs in check-only mode and a read probe under app_service against the restored instance (extend scripts/ops/dr-application-readiness.mjs so it is not limited to dr_proof.*).
   c. Restore one noncurrent vault object version and verify its SHA-256 against vault.documents.
   d. Record measured RPO/RTO and delete the temporary instance in an always() step.
   Also align the fixture drill's container to postgres:15 to match RDS.
7. Tests, made to fail first: add terraform tests (terraform/stack/tests/dr.tftest.hcl) asserting the backup plan has copy_action to the DR region, the vault lock exists, both buckets have replication rules, and replica keys exist for database, vault and release_signing. Run them at HEAD and record the failures.
8. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: (a) The new terraform tests fail at HEAD (no backup plan, replication or replica keys) and pass after. (b) The staging PITR drill workflow completes green and uploads evidence with restore start and finish timestamps, observed RPO and RTO, the migration level of the restored DB, an app_service read probe result, and one restored vault object whose hash matches vault.documents. (c) The drill is shown failing once by pointing it at a nonexistent restore time or a corrupted object hash. (d) The RPO/RTO and owner rows in docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md are filled and approved. (e) aws backup list-recovery-points-by-backup-vault in the DR region shows copies within 24 h of first apply.
records.dependencies: Founder: DR region, RPO/RTO, retention, approvers. A first AWS apply and a staging environment in AWS (deploy-aws.yml has 0 runs; WO-4 staging promotion). Key multi-region changes must land before the first apply.

records.title: SOC 2 AWS baseline still absent: no GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, VPC flow logs, ALB/CloudFront/S3 access logs, WAF or budgets
records.evidenceAtHead: Repo-wide grep for aws_guardduty, aws_securityhub, aws_config_, aws_flow_log, aws_wafv2, aws_budgets, logging_config and aws_s3_bucket_logging in *.tf: no hits. terraform/modules/alb/variables.tf:40-43: access_logs_bucket still defaults to "" (alb/main.tf:41-44 enabled = var.access_logs_bucket != ""), and terraform/stack/main.tf:363-374 module "alb" does not pass it. terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:149-156 still says 'No WAF yet: a founder decision', with #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 on the distribution and no logging_config. terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf resources (lines 4-132) include no flow log. terraform/bootstrap/ holds only main.tf and variables.tf, with none of these. The only detective controls at HEAD are the CloudTrail multi-region trail (compliance-evidence/main.tf:316), RDS logs and pgaudit (rds/main.tf:61, 116-120). Both existed or are DB-level and are not part of this finding.
records.remaining: All listed controls: GuardDuty (including ECS runtime, S3 and RDS protection), Security Hub with FSBP and CIS, AWS Config recorder, VPC flow logs, ALB access logs, CloudFront and S3 server access logging, WAF (count mode first) and budgets with alerts.
records.severityRationale: A design partner's security questionnaire will ask for threat detection and edge or access logs. More concretely, without ALB, CloudFront or flow logs and GuardDuty, a pilot-era incident cannot be scoped, which is a data-integrity and legal exposure for GxP records. GuardDuty, access logs, flow logs and budgets are cheap and are P1. Security Hub and Config scoring, and switching WAF from count to block, can be P2 for GA.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decisions: whether staging and prod share one AWS account (this decides where account-level resources live), WAF budget and posture, budget ceiling and alert recipients.
2. Account-level controls go in terraform/bootstrap/main.tf, or in a new terraform/modules/security-baseline instantiated once per account behind var.manage_account_baseline. Do not instantiate them per environment in a shared account. They are:
   a. aws_guardduty_detector with features S3_DATA_EVENTS, RDS_LOGIN_EVENTS and RUNTIME_MONITORING (ECS_FARGATE_AGENT_MANAGEMENT).
   b. aws_securityhub_account plus aws_securityhub_standards_subscription for AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and CIS AWS Foundations.
   c. aws_config_configuration_recorder (all supported resources), aws_config_delivery_channel to a dedicated, KMS-encrypted log bucket, and aws_config_configuration_recorder_status enabled.
   d. aws_budgets_budget, monthly COST, with 80% and 100% notifications to the named recipients.
3. VPC flow logs: in terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf, add an aws_cloudwatch_log_group (KMS-encrypted, 365-day retention), an IAM role and aws_flow_log { vpc_id = aws_vpc.this.id, traffic_type = "ALL" }.
4. ALB access logs:
   a. In terraform/stack, create a log bucket. Use SSE-S3, because ALB access logs do not support SSE-KMS. Add a public-access block, lifecycle retention, and a bucket policy allowing logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com (or the region's ELB account) to PutObject under AWSLogs/<account>/.
   b. Pass access_logs_bucket into module "alb" at terraform/stack/main.tf:363-374.
   c. Add a stack precondition that production sets it.
5. CloudFront and S3 logging:
   a. Add a logging_config block to aws_cloudfront_distribution.this (cloudfront/main.tf:157). Its target bucket needs ACLs enabled (BucketOwnerPreferred). Alternatively use CloudFront v2 logging via aws_cloudwatch_log_delivery_source/destination/delivery.
   b. Add aws_s3_bucket_logging for the vault bucket (vault_storage.tf) and the frontend bucket to a separate log bucket.
   c. Never set the evidence bucket's logging target to itself. compliance-evidence/main.tf:1-15 documents the recursive-logging loop already fixed once.
6. WAF:
   a. Add aws_wafv2_web_acl with scope CLOUDFRONT, created through a us-east-1 provider alias. Include AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with override_action { count {} }, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, and a rate-based rule on /api/auth/*.
   b. Set web_acl_id on the distribution.
   c. Delete the #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 and the 'No WAF yet' comment at cloudfront/main.tf:149-156 in the same change.
   d. Only after reviewing counted matches against document uploads (bodies over 8 KB) and AnA turns, switch to block with a SizeRestrictions_BODY scope-down exclusion.
7. Tests, made to fail first:
   a. Add tftest runs: modules/vpc-secure/tests asserting the flow log, modules/alb/tests asserting access_logs.enabled = true when a bucket is passed, the stack test asserting production passes a non-empty access_logs_bucket, cloudfront tests asserting logging_config and web_acl_id, and a security-baseline module test.
   b. Run them at HEAD and record the failures.
   c. Move terraform-compliance.yml (Checkov) to trigger on push to concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0 means no PRs), so these controls stay gated.
8. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: (a) The new tftest runs fail at HEAD and pass after the change. (b) After apply: aws guardduty create-sample-findings produces a finding visible in Security Hub, and the Security Hub FSBP and CIS scores are exported to docs/evidence. (c) Flow-log, ALB and CloudFront log objects appear within 15 minutes of a smoke test. (d) A budget notification test fires to the named recipient. (e) WAF count-mode metrics show requests evaluated, and a 9 KB vault upload still succeeds.
records.dependencies: Founder decisions on account layout, WAF budget and budget ceiling. A first AWS apply (deploy-aws.yml has 0 runs). Relates to OPS-18 (Checkov dormant under Rule 0).

records.title: API task still carries the RDS master (owner) DATABASE_URL and APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD; boot DDL and one route still run on the owner connection
records.evidenceAtHead: terraform/stack/main.tf:39-48 calls DATABASE_URL the owner role, used by migrations and by the API at boot, and labels it 'A known exposure'. main.tf:93 builds database_url from module.rds.master_username and random_password.db_master. main.tf:315-316: DATABASE_URL is in local.boot_secrets, which feeds both api_secrets (line 431) and worker_secrets (line 440). main.tf:432 adds APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD to the API task. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514 preflight REQUIRES DATABASE_URL in the API container. scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh:68-92 derives the migrate task by cloning the API's checked revision, which is why the owner secrets sit in the API definition. Runtime owner use: server/startup/services.ts:130 ensureCoreTables(process.env.DATABASE_URL) runs CREATE SCHEMA/EXTENSION/TABLE (server/db/ensureCoreTables.ts:348-541). server/startup/services.ts:278-279 ensureAuthTables opens an owner Pool (server/db/bootstrap/index.ts:33-43) for DDL plus seeds. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-75 builds a postgres() client on DATABASE_URL that serves /api/tenants requests outside RLS. server/startup/env.ts:66-68 makes DATABASE_URL mandatory at boot. Rotation (5ef2787a5, var.db_credentials_rotation) changes the password, not who holds it.
records.remaining: The API (and worker) task definitions still receive the master or owner URL and the app_service password. The API still runs DDL at boot and serves tenants-simple routes through an owner client. The deploy preflight still requires the owner URL in the API task, and the migrate task is still derived from the API definition.
records.severityRationale: An RCE or SSRF-to-env leak in the web tier yields the RDS master credential: owner of every table, RLS bypassed, able to drop the audit tables. That defeats tenant isolation and Part 11 audit immutability in one step. The tenants-simple route also runs live requests through the owner connection, so a logic bug there bypasses RLS without needing RCE. It needs a preceding compromise or bug, so P1 rather than P0, but it must be closed before pilot data lands.
records.instructions:
1. Move boot DDL into the migration set (Rule 1).
   a. Translate every CREATE SCHEMA/EXTENSION/TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in server/db/ensureCoreTables.ts (about lines 395-541) and in server/db/bootstrap/auth-schema.ts (applyAuthSchemaMigrations, applyModuleCatalogSchema) into additive, IF NOT EXISTS-guarded migration files.
   b. Append them to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs, before the final RLS sweep pair (ci:migration-set-order enforces that).
   c. Tables that already exist keep their shape. Any genuinely new table goes in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL.
   d. Move seedOrganizations into a migration using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with a row-count assertion. Make seedGaDemoUser (server/db/bootstrap/seed-default-org.ts:138) refuse to run when NODE_ENV=production.
   e. Run npm run ci:migration-drop-safety and ci:migration-set-order.
2. Make API boot read-only on the runtime role.
   a. server/startup/services.ts:130: call a verify-only variant of ensureCoreTables (no DDL) on getRuntimeDatabaseUrl().
   b. server/startup/services.ts:278-279: replace ensureAuthTables() with a schema-presence check that reports readiness 'error' when columns are missing.
   c. Keep the DDL paths reachable only from scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs.
   d. server/startup/env.ts:66-68: in production require APP_DATABASE_URL and do NOT require DATABASE_URL.
3. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-75: delete the module-level postgres() owner client and serve the routes through the runtime pool. Use runWithSystemTenantScope for platform-admin estate reads and the org-scoped connection for tenant reads, as the rest of server/routes does. Keep server/__tests__/security/tenant-isolation-tenants-simple.contract.test.ts passing. server/services/ana-cortex-service.ts:57 only inspects the string: change it to report APP_DATABASE_URL presence.
4. Terraform.
   a. terraform/stack/main.tf:315-316: remove DATABASE_URL from local.boot_secrets. Add local.owner_secrets = [DATABASE_URL, APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD].
   b. Remove APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD from api_secrets (line 432).
   c. In terraform/modules/ecs-fargate, add aws_ecs_task_definition.migrate (family ${cluster_name}-migrate, one container, no clamav sidecar) whose secrets are boot_secrets plus owner_secrets.
   d. Give the migrate definition its own execution role, allowed GetSecretValue on the owner secret ARNs. Remove those ARNs from the API execution role's policy (ecs-fargate/main.tf:51-73) by splitting var.secret_arns into api and migrate lists.
   e. Add the migrate execution role to pass_role_arns and the migrate family to one_off_task_families in modules/github-deploy-roles (main.tf:104-112).
   f. Add ignore_changes on the image field only if the deploy registers revisions of it.
5. scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh:68-92: derive the one-off task from the Terraform-owned migrate family's latest revision with only the image replaced by the checked digest, instead of from the API revision. Keep the ARN race check in deploy-aws.yml.
6. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514-541 preflight:
   a. Remove DATABASE_URL from the required list for the API container.
   b. Add a refusal when the API container carries DATABASE_URL or APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD.
   c. Add a separate check that the migrate family carries both.
   d. Update the comment at lines 443-449.
   e. Extend scripts/ops/terraform-preflight-proof.mjs with a negative fixture (an API task definition carrying DATABASE_URL) and show the preflight refusing it.
7. Tests, made to fail first:
   a. Add a run to terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl asserting the API container's secret names include neither DATABASE_URL nor APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD and that the migrate definition includes both. Run it at HEAD and record the failure (main.tf:316, 432).
   b. In ci.yml's production boot smoke, unset DATABASE_URL for the dist/index.js boot and require /readyz=200.
8. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase. Removing ensureAuthTables' boot path is not a capability deletion: name scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs and the new migration files as the replacement in the commit message.
records.acceptance: (a) The boot_contract tftest run asserting no owner secrets in the API container fails at HEAD and passes after. (b) terraform-preflight-proof.mjs shows the preflight refusing an API task definition that carries DATABASE_URL, and accepting the Terraform-rendered one. (c) The CI production boot smoke reaches /readyz=200 with DATABASE_URL unset and APP_DATABASE_URL as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role. (d) grep -rn "process.env.DATABASE_URL" server --include=*.ts (excluding tests) returns only migration/CLI code, not startup/services.ts or routes/tenants-simple.ts. (e) The tenant-isolation tenants-simple contract test passes. (f) The blank-DB CI job proves deploy-migrate alone creates every table ensureCoreTables used to create.
records.dependencies: None blocking; it touches the D1 boot contract and deploy-aws.yml preflight, so coordinate with the OPS-11/WO-9 launch-config lane. Rule 1 migration-set gates must stay green.
